title: Drop and Deadline
premise: August Lockridge, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, receives a call on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — the voice belongs to their presumed-dead mentor, Elias Vane, who claims the inheritance August never knew they were owed is the key to stopping an assassination at an upcoming diplomatic summit. As August follows Elias's trail through a web of rewritten rules, double-crossed handlers, and a rival contractor who was once the love of their life, they discover the 'secret worth killing for' is proof that August's own employer orchestrated the plot. In the end, August must choose between delivering the evidence to save their career and burning it to protect the person they love, ultimately leaking it publicly and walking away from the life of duty that defined them — finding belonging not in an institution, but in the choice to stay.
about_author: Beatrix Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she can no longer name. She now writes thrillers from a coastal cottage, where she insists her security system is a very judgmental dog.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: August's POV. Working a routine protection detail in Geneva, August finds a burner phone sewn into their go-bag — a bag only one person ever packed for them. When it rings, Elias Vane's voice, dead for three years, gives them thirty seconds of instructions before the line dies. The beat: dread laced with grief reawakened.

chapters.title: Rules Written in Pencil
chapters.summary: August's POV. August verifies the voice against old mission recordings and discovers their employer, Meridian Protective Group, has quietly scrubbed every file connecting them to Elias. Their handler, Corrigan, assigns them to the summit detail with suspicious urgency. The beat: the ground shifting under everything August believed.

chapters.title: What the Dead Owe Us
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, flashbacks interleaved with present. Three years ago, Elias faked his death after discovering Meridian's founder was selling access to summit intelligence; he hid the proof inside an inheritance he routed to August's name. Present-day Elias watches August from a rooftop, unable to make contact. The beat: tragic devotion.

chapters.title: Old Flame, New Contract
chapters.summary: August's POV. At a pre-summit reception, August runs into Nadia Reyes — rival contractor, former lover, now head of the opposing security team. Their charged sparring masks mutual recognition that something is wrong with this assignment. That night, someone searches August's room. The beat: longing sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following Elias's instructions to a Zurich vault, August learns the 'inheritance' is a data core containing Meridian's assassination plan targeting a whistleblower delegate at the summit. Before they can leave, Meridian's cleaners arrive. August escapes with help from an anonymous texter: Nadia. The beat: hunted, and no longer alone.

chapters.title: Two Guns, One Safehouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, August and Nadia. Holed up together, they trade truths: Nadia was hired by the delegate herself, who suspects her own government. Old love resurfaces between interrogations, but August hides the data core's existence — duty versus trust made flesh. The beat: intimacy rebuilt on half-confessions.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corrigan's POV. We learn Corrigan has been feeding Elias information for years, torn between loyalty to Meridian's founder and guilt over operatives already silenced. Ordered to bring August in 'off the books,' Corrigan instead warns them — and pays for it. The beat: a good man complicit, finally choosing.

chapters.title: Drop and Deadline
chapters.summary: August's POV. Elias finally surfaces in person, but the reunion curdles: he admits he used August as a courier all along, betting their inheritance claim would force Meridian's hand. Meridian's strike team hits the safehouse; Elias takes a bullet covering August's escape. The beat: betrayal and sacrifice fused.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. With the summit convening, August infiltrates the venue carrying the data core, outmaneuvers both Meridian's killers and their own extraction orders, and exposes the plot mid-session with Nadia running interference. The founder is arrested; the delegate lives. The beat: love against duty, resolved by choosing both.

chapters.title: Belonging, Rewritten
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. Weeks later, August declines reinstatement, testifies anonymously, and buries Elias beside the sea he loved. Nadia arrives unannounced with two tickets and no itinerary. August locks the burner phone in a drawer, keeps the door unlocked. The beat: quiet peace earned, belonging chosen rather than assigned.
